clue.text: Archdeacon returning to a tribe as US resident

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for the archdeacon's title is read backwards

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title given to an archdeacon
Dan is one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: A senior churchman goes back to a tribe, now living in America.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven; reversed this gives NEV.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in the state of Nevada is a Nevadan, so one kind of US resident.

clue.text: Monster that is spotted south of headland

indicators.note: in a down clue, being seen south of something puts it underneath, so after

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Scottish place names
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A creature sighted below a promontory.
explanation.walkthrough: IE goes below NESS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the nickname of the legendary Loch Ness monster.

clue.text: Men in street returning after farewell

indicators.note: after places the turned-around street abbreviation behind the farewell

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

indicators.note: returning means the street abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: Men in a road going home after saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Valets are manservants, so men in the sense of servants.

clue.text: Party with small booze containers for the monks

parts.note: a do is a party
mini means small
cans hold beer and other drink

explanation.surface: A party with little tins of drink laid on for the brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominicans are friars of the Order of Preachers founded by St Dominic, a religious order.

clue.text: Man said brief word of farewell at end of day

definitions.text: brief word of farewell at end of day

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken, so we hear the chess piece

parts.note: a knight is a man in chess

explanation.surface: A man uttered a quick goodbye as evening fell.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess pieces are called men; the knight, spoken, loses its silent K.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'Night!' is a clipped form of goodnight, used when parting late in the day.

clue.text: Cook has little time left to join in ceremonial feast

indicators.note: to join in tells us the two short pieces go into the middle of the cooking word

parts.note: to poach is to cook gently in liquid
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A chef with barely a moment to spare helps out at a grand ceremonial banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling of this feast has a second T; the version here is an accepted variant.
explanation.definitionFit: A potlatch is a gift-giving festival held by Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest, a ceremonial feast.

clue.text: Cop having to get round? Simple with quality car

parts.note: pat means glib or simple, as in a pat answer
Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A policeman with a beat to cover, glibly joined by a luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Roller' is British slang for a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: A patroller goes round an area on patrol, as a police officer on the beat does.

clue.text: Peg, little wife held to be quaint

indicators.note: held means the abbreviation for wife is gripped inside the peg word

parts.note: a tee is a golfer's peg
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A small wife named Peg considered charmingly old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' looks like a woman's name but is the golf tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is British for affectedly dainty or cutesy, overly quaint.

clue.text: Excellent waste pipe trapping carbon pollutant

indicators.note: trapping means the carbon symbol is caught within the other pieces

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with the numeral as the letter I
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
a drain carries waste water away

explanation.surface: A fine sewer pipe holding carbon that dirties the environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent' is A1, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is precipitation made acidic by sulphur and nitrogen emissions, an environmental pollutant.

clue.text: Fellow in criminal activity as one looking for kicks

indicators.note: in means the fellow word goes inside the crime word

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A college fellow mixed up in crime for the thrill of it.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university teacher, often called a fellow at Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist pursues pleasure above all, a thrill-seeker.

clue.text: Men switching sides in a city of trials

indicators.note: switching sides means the letters at the two ends trade places

parts.note: males are men

explanation.surface: Men changing allegiance in a town known for its courtroom dramas.
explanation.walkthrough: In MALES the first and last letters, M and S, swap ends to give the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Salem, Massachusetts, is famous for the witch trials of 1692.

clue.text: Lose time offering support

definitions.meaning: to ... a cause is to back it

explanation.surface: Falling behind schedule while trying to be helpful.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to fall into arrears and, figuratively, to back or champion someone.

clue.text: Way of speaking not unusual in one country

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged word between the numeral and the country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a country

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of the word not are jumbled

explanation.surface: A manner of talking that is quite ordinary within a single nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' looks like it qualifies the way of speaking, but it signals the jumble of 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice, a characteristic manner of speaking.

clue.text: Eagle shortly crossing island, a poetic land

indicators.note: crossing means the shortened bird goes around the island letter
shortly means the bird's name loses its final letter

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle

explanation.surface: A bird flies briefly over an island in a land of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims ERNE to ERN, which goes around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is the old poetic name for Ireland.

clue.text: Sail with a thousand on a cruise at sea

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sailing with a thousand others on a cruise in open water.
explanation.definitionFit: On a square-rigged ship the course is the lowest sail on a mast, the main course on the mainmast.

clue.text: Tubes bringing a form of medication to stop decay

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, so the medication sits inside the decay word

parts.note: caries is tooth decay
a pill is one form of medicine

explanation.surface: Tubes deliver a remedy to halt tooth rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' means to plug a gap, so the medication fills the decay, as a dentist would.
explanation.definitionFit: Capillaries are the finest blood vessels, tiny tubes in the body.

clue.text: One may give smashing Yule report with no end of turkey supplied?

definitions.text: One may give smashing Yule report with no end of turkey supplied?

indicators.note: smashing means the letters of the two words are broken up and rebuilt
no end of means the final letter of the bird is taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: Someone may deliver a glowing Christmas report about the turkey they sold.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange YULE REPORT less Y, the last letter of turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A poulterer deals in poultry, so is the person who supplies a Christmas turkey.

clue.text: Noticed upturned furniture item fit for the skip?

indicators.note: upturned in a down clue means the seeing word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: saw means noticed
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: An overturned piece of furniture is spotted, ready for throwing out.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the British term for a large rubbish container, a dumpster.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wastable may be thrown away, so is fit for dumping in a rubbish container.

clue.text: Kid in ruin needing a bit of money in Bulgaria

indicators.note: in means the child word goes inside the ruin word

parts.note: to sink a plan is to ruin it
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A child in ruin needs a little cash in Bulgaria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' is a verb here: to scupper or sink a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: The stotinka is the Bulgarian coin worth a hundredth of a lev, a small unit of currency.

clue.text: Subatomic particle in nature not transformed

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of the three words are reshaped into something new

explanation.surface: A tiny particle found in the natural world, unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' looks like science-speak for the particle, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An antineutron is the antimatter counterpart of the neutron, a subatomic particle.

clue.text: Is head of French in university an oddball?

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the university's initials

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of the word French

explanation.surface: Is the leading French scholar at a university an eccentric?
explanation.walkthrough: The university is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit does not fit in with others, an odd or eccentric person.

clue.text: Home nurse being mean

parts.note: in means at home
to tend is to nurse

explanation.surface: A district nurse is being stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb, to have in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to mean to do something, to have it as one's purpose.

clue.text: Irish poet contributing to event at Easter

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer from Ireland takes part in a springtime festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is hidden across 'evenT AT Easter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum Tate, born in Dublin, was Poet Laureate and wrote the libretto for Dido and Aeneas.

clue.text: Outside shelter there's rain so terribly loud and powerful

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters wrap around the shelter word
terribly tells us the letters of rain and so are scrambled

parts.note: a tent is a shelter

explanation.surface: Camping in a downpour that is awfully loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' gives SORIAN from RAIN SO, which goes 'Outside' TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentorian describes a booming voice, after Stentor, the herald in the Iliad.

clue.text: This person in hospital sent up labels

indicators.note: in means the speaker's pronoun goes inside the hospital word
sent up in a down clue means the hospital word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a san is a sanatorium
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: The setter, in a hospital, mocks the labels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' looks like mockery but in a down clue means read upwards; a san is a sanatorium.
explanation.definitionFit: Names are the words used to identify things, as labels are.

clue.text: The measure of a Labour leader

definitions.meaning: a unit of length of twelve inches
Michael ... led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983

explanation.surface: Taking the measure of a Labour Party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an imperial unit of length and the surname of Michael Foot, a leader of Britain's Labour Party.

clue.text: Good foreign deity with strange instrument

parts.note: bon is French for good
a god is a deity
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A kindly foreign god comes with an unusual musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' in British English means peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bongo drum is one of a pair of small hand-played drums, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Weapon in sack

definitions.meaning: to sack is to plunder, to ransack

explanation.surface: A gun stashed in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a long gun and also a verb meaning to search through and steal from.

clue.text: Demanding type, discarded player

parts.note: ex means former, cast off
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A difficult person, a performer who has been dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: One who exacts, insisting on payment or obedience, is a demanding sort.

clue.text: Horse keeping dry, put back as before

indicators.note: keeping means the horse word holds the abstaining letters inside it

parts.note: a steed is a horse
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol, so dry

explanation.surface: A horse that stays off the drink is returned to how it was.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, for teetotal, is the crossword's usual way of saying dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is a proofreader's mark meaning let the original stand, so a stetted text is restored.
